Subject: Unit economics deep-dive: $/feature, CAC payback & target $/1M tokens (CareHealth)

Great to chat earlier — quick recap and a proposed follow-up plan. Thanks, Alyssa, for walking through CareHealth’s usage profile. Below are the assumptions I captured; please correct anything that’s off.

Call highlights / confirmed inputs
- Primary feature: automated patient intake convo + summarization (embedded in clinician UI).
- Estimated monthly active users (MAU): 45k
- Avg tokens per session (round-trip prompts + responses + KV): 1,200 tokens
- Expected sessions per MAU per month: 3
- Pilot horizon: 3 months, national rollout after Q4 if pilot meets latency/cost SLAs
- Budget range (initial): $8k–$35k/month (you mentioned procurement anchors around $20k)

Immediate asks (from Redwood)
1) Confirm the 45k MAU and 1,200 tokens/session (or send a sample logs export).
2) Which metric matters most for procurement: $/1M tokens, $/feature, or cost per MAU?
3) Any procurement timing constraints or approval windows we should design the pilot around?

What we’ll deliver by EOD Monday
- A 1-page unit-econ sketch showing $/1M-token bands (three pricing bands: pilot, committed, enterprise)
- $/feature estimate for the targeted patient-intake flow (assumptions line-itemed)
- CAC payback quick model given your current ASP & churn assumptions that you provided

Attached: carehealth_token_model_v2.xlsx — editable assumptions sheet.

If that aligns I’ll loop in Solutions (Ben) to produce the $/feature sketch and Marissa to propose a pilot billing structure.

Best,

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Park <alyssa@carehealth.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-15T08:22:00Z
Subject: RE: Unit economics deep-dive: $/feature, CAC payback & target $/1M tokens (CareHealth)

Hi all — putting a quick sketch in the thread so we have a baseline before we lock numbers in the spreadsheet. Assumptions used (editable in the attached workbook):
- Monthly sessions = MAU * sessions_per_MAU = 45,000 * 3 = 135,000 sessions/month
- Token mix (weighted avg tokens/session) = 0.6*400 + 0.3*1200 + 0.1*3500 = 976 tokens/session ~ 1k
- Monthly tokens = 135,000 * 976 ≈ 132M tokens/month

Price band sketch (Redwood list; final depends on commit & latency SLO):
- Pilot (no commit, burst-cap): $35 / 1M tokens (pilot SLA: best-effort; throttling at peak)
- Committed startup band (6mo, 1–2M tokens/day committed): $18 / 1M tokens
- Enterprise reserved (annual commit + SLOs): $9–12 / 1M tokens depending on quantization & batching profiles

$/feature (patient-intake flow) — cost to Redwood (rough)
- Avg tokens/feature = 1,000
- At $18 / 1M tokens -> cost per feature = $0.018
- At $12 / 1M tokens -> cost per feature = $0.012
- At pilot $35 / 1M tokens -> cost per feature = $0.035

CAC payback sketch (very rough):
- Assume ASP per account (clinic site) = $1,200/month net subscription for the feature set
- Average gross margin (software) target = 65% post-inference costs excluded
- Inference cost impact per account (MAU per account assumed 250 users) => inference delta = 250 users * 3 sessions * 1000 tokens * 30 days ≈ 22.5M tokens/month -> at $18/1M = $405/month in inference cost
- If net revenue per account = $1,200 * 0.65 = $780 gross margin, inference at $405 consumes ~52% of margin — too high.

What this implies:
- To meet a healthy margin target (60–70% contribution margin after infra), we need either lower $/1M (enterprise reserved range) or higher price per account.
- Alternatively, Redwood can propose feature-tiering: lightweight triage model (lower-cost quantized variant) for 60% of sessions, standard model for longer sessions. That can cut blended $/1M by ~25–40% depending on split.

Next steps (proposal)
1) We produce a 1-page two-track pilot proposal: (A) Pilot capped at $20k/month for 3 months (no commit), (B) Committed 6-month tier: $15 / 1M tokens with a 20% usage discount after commit.
2) CareHealth to confirm sessions MAU distribution and sample logs (to refine the token mix).
3) If both align, Marissa drafts a short pilot addendum and pricing term sheet for procurement.

Attaching: redwood-inference-pricing.xlsx (banded pricing table).

—
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Unit economics deep-dive: $/feature, CAC payback & target $/1M tokens (CareHealth)

Alyssa — thanks for the quick clarifications. Based on Ben’s sketch I’ve drafted two practical pilots to present to procurement and execs:

Pilot A — Cost-capped evaluation (lowest friction)
- Term: 3 months
- Max monthly cost: $20,000 (hard cap)
- Service level: standard API; throughput best-effort; we’ll include a mitigation clause if sustained throttling occurs
- Deliverables: latency report, cost-per-session breakdown weekly, token usage dashboard access
- Pricing during pilot: $35 / 1M tokens charged up to cap (we absorb overage % if engineering issue on our side)

Pilot B — Committed throughput pilot (predictable economics)
- Term: 6 months
- Commit: 12M tokens/day average (or equivalent monthly commit)
- Pricing: $15 / 1M tokens for committed volume, 20% overage discount slab after commit
- Deliverables: guaranteed latency SLO (P95 < 400ms), priority support, pilot success playbook

Recommended ask from CareHealth: commit to Pilot B if you can approve the 6-month window — it gives you ~2–3x lower inference cost at scale. If procurement needs lower short-term risk, Pilot A gets you started with a cap.

Marissa will prepare the pilot addendum + MSA link (DocuSign) once we get confirmation of which pilot you prefer. I’ve attached a signed copy of our standard MSA tracker for reference.

Action items: Alyssa/procurement to confirm preferred pilot option and send sample logs (or allow SFTP pull). We’ll finalize numbers in the attached carehealth_token_model_v2.xlsx.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Head, Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
